body.claim: In 1980, hard drives that could store more than a gigabyte already existed. IBM's 3380 held 2.52 GB.
body.why: IBM introduced the 3380 on 11 June 1980. NEC's N7755, also from 1980, held 1.27 GB. Both were early drives in the gigabyte era.

probes.question: True or false: hard drives holding more than a gigabyte already existed in 1980.

sources.title: History of IBM magnetic disk drives (Wikipedia)

image_brief.show: A 1980s IBM disk drive or a room of mainframe storage

claims.claim: In 1980, IBM's 3380 became the first hard drive to hold a gigabyte.
claims.quote: was the first hard disk drive to ship with a capacity exceeding 1 gigabyte (GB) capacity, with 1.27 GB storage
claims.note: The NEC N7755 (1980, 1.27 GB) is credited as first >1 GB; IBM 3380 was 2.52 GB, introduced June 11, 1980. Suggest: "In 1980, IBM's 3380 was one of the first drives to exceed a gigabyte (2.52 GB)".

claims.claim: A modern phone holds hundreds of times that capacity in a few grams.
A microSD card holds far more than the 3380 did.
claims.note: Not in fetched text; 3380 capacity 2.52 GB is stated at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_IBM_magnetic_disk_drives.

claims.claim: Probe: the first gigabyte-sized hard drive (1980) weighed about 250 kg (true).
claims.note: Premise attributes first-gigabyte to the 3380 and weight is unsourced; do not mark true until sourced.
